verificationSummary: Editor merge commit a11db59634873d309a0fb469a6479a099705a28e fixes the bounded selection overlay zoom motion lag reported from the Editor design view. Root cause scope was presentation-only: the selected paper block animates with the scaled paper during viewport-only zoom, while the separate canvas selection overlay previously measured once and then waited for a settle timeout, leaving a visible stale outline before the next geometry update. Pre-fix browser sampling on http://127.0.0.1:4001/documents/product-report-vnext-minimal/design measured stale overlay divergence during 85% to 95% zoom with max delta about 60.47px. Focused RED failed in src/tests/selectionOverlay.test.ts because no animation-frame overlay sync was scheduled, then failed again because applySelectionOverlayStyle was not implemented or used by CanvasOverlayLayer. The Editor fix schedules 24 animation-frame syncs during zoom motion, keeps the existing 180ms settle sync, and applies measured overlay CSS variables directly to the mounted outline element before React's next render. Focused GREEN passed npx vitest run src/tests/selectionOverlay.test.ts --reporter verbose with 1 file and 9 tests. Editor worktree npm run check passed type-check, 88 passed test files, 305 passed tests, and build. Worktree browser evidence on http://127.0.0.1:4042/documents/product-report-vnext-minimal/design measured 85% to 95% max overlay delta 0.014px. Merged Editor main npm run check passed type-check, 88 passed test files, 305 passed tests, and build. Main browser evidence on http://127.0.0.1:4001/documents/product-report-vnext-minimal/design with Backend on http://127.0.0.1:4011 measured 85% to 95% max overlay delta 0.011px. Vite still reports the existing chunk-size warning. The Editor npm install in the lane reported 5 high severity vulnerabilities. git deregistered the Editor worktree and deleted the merged branch, but the residual .worktrees/editor-selection-overlay-zoom-motion-sync folder could not be removed because the local command policy blocked recursive deletion. This evidence supports only the bounded Editor selection overlay zoom motion bugfix and does not promote broad Editor truth, WYSIWYG readiness, text input readiness, command authoring readiness, Backend mutation or persistence readiness, Backend production readiness, Core truth, accessibility readiness, visual regression readiness, durable storage readiness, PDF export readiness, bundle-size readiness, live production behavior, or FlowDoc product readiness.
